title: hopeium issue
description: A hopeium issue per the hopeium capability specification's media line (iv) and the hopeium-media note's plan (3.1): a continuation reading rendered as newsletter-issue-production's own issue shape, profiled with the four fields the plan names and no `verdict` field. A thin allOf profile: branch one copies, by path (never by $ref — @red-cup-engineering/newsletter-issue-production-services-section 0.1.0's src/newsletter-issue.mjs `validateIssue` declares no $id to $ref), the base issue shape {title, dek, sections, references} that package's renderer actually enforces, left open at the top level (it is not this profile's to close); branch two adds claim/lament/continuation/return, permissively admits the base's own field names (so its own additionalProperties:false does not reject them — see 2026-09-06's admitted friction on this same evaluator's lack of unevaluatedProperties, named on territory-catalog-row.schema.json beside this file), and is the branch that refuses a `verdict` key. Structural shape only: the settled-outcome-on-open-cell and no-return format refusals are business rules the checker (scripts/check-hopeium-issue.mjs) applies on top, not expressible cleanly as a cross-field JSON Schema keyword this evaluator supports.

allOf.description: Copied by path from newsletter-issue-production-services-section's src/newsletter-issue.mjs validateIssue (title/dek/sections/references and their per-item shape); left open (no additionalProperties:false here) because closing it is this base's renderer's concern, not this profile's.

The hopeium profile's own fields (hopeium-media note 3.1). Closes the top-level object against additionalProperties:false so a `verdict` key is refused; the base's four field names are listed permissively (`true`) purely so this branch's own closure does not reject them, never redefining their shape (branch one owns that).

claim.description: A FOUR-valued claim with provenance, the plan's held cell.

lament.description: Complaint within relation: grief and protest addressed to the Holder, without closure in either direction (2026-08-23 abandonment note §4.3) — never a verdict.

continuation.description: A record-level continuation reading (hopeium-media note 3.3): a cited record with evidence rows and a next step, or the literal none-found with the search that was run. Never the unbuilt-affects chronicle formalization, which is blocked upstream.

recordPath.description: Repo-relative path to the record carrying the evidence rows.

items.description: One evidence row in @red-cup-engineering/derive-continuation-reading-service's request evidence-row shape (its ContinuationReadingRequest candidate.evidenceRows item), so the checker can build a one-candidate reading request straight from this continuation.

evidenceRows.description: Evidence rows within recordPath that this continuation cites as evidence, in the derive-continuation-reading-service request shape.

searched.description: What was searched, so 'none found' is itself first-class output, never a bare closure.

return.description: The reader returned: a longer reading, a body practice, a person to tell (the founder's own practice list). `reading` is structurally optional here — its presence is the checker's NO_RETURN business rule, not a schema-level requirement, so the two are independently testable.
